version.changelog: Fix metadata: clarify no Polymarket connection, add The Odds API source URL, improve description accuracy

llm.summary: This sports-odds scanner is mostly purpose-aligned, but it handles an API key and automated file writes in ways users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Use of ODDS_API_KEY is expected for live odds, but the key is sent as a query parameter and raw request exceptions are logged, which can copy the key into stdout or scheduler logs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest installs the expected Python dependency, requests, but leaves it unpinned and does not declare narrow runtime permission scopes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents the external API, relevant environment variables, default results path, and output behavior, but it does not clearly warn that HTTP error logging may expose the odds API key.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The managed automaton runs every 30 minutes and writes to RESULTS_FILE; persistence is disclosed, but the path is fully environment-controlled and can overwrite any file the process can write.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The code matches the stated purpose: it fetches sports odds from The Odds API, detects arbitrage, logs opportunities, and saves JSON results; the Polymarket name mismatch is disclosed in the skill text.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing if you will use a real ODDS_API_KEY. Run it only in an environment where scheduler/stdout logs are private, consider rotating any key exposed in logs, set RESULTS_FILE to a dedicated safe path, and prefer a version that redacts apiKey values and pins dependencies.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Sending ODDS_API_KEY to The Odds API is necessary for live odds and is not evidence of unrelated exfiltration, but the query-parameter credential plus raw exception logging creates a real exposure risk.
[LP3] unexpected: Network access, environment reads, and file writes are coherent with the skill, but the artifact lacks explicit narrow permission declarations for those capabilities.
[E1] expected: The external URL is the documented odds provider and matches the stated source, so this network transmission is purpose-aligned.
[TT2] expected: Writing results to disk is documented and expected, but accepting an unrestricted RESULTS_FILE path creates file-clobbering risk if the environment is misconfigured or attacker-controlled.
[TT2] expected: The empty-results write path has the same unrestricted RESULTS_FILE behavior, even though it writes only an empty JSON array.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistence of results is disclosed in SKILL.md, including the default path, so this is expected behavior; the remaining concern is lack of path containment or confirmation.
[T09] unexpected: The AIG finding is supported: raw RequestException logging after raise_for_status can include the prepared URL containing apiKey.
[T08] unexpected: The AIG dependency note is supported: requests is legitimate and expected, but unpinned.
